## Question 2.1: Loading and preparing the news documents

```{r}
# Find the text files within the sa_news folder
news_files <- list.files(
  path = "sa_news",
  pattern = "\\.txt$",
  full.names = TRUE
)

# Create one row per file, containing the name and full text
news_data <- data.frame(
  file_name = basename(news_files),
  content = vapply(
    news_files,
    function(file){
      paste(readLines(file, warn = FALSE, encoding = "UTF-8"),
            collapse = " ")
    },
    character(1)
  ),
  stringAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Check to see how many documents were loaded 
nrow(news_data)

# View file names and beginning of each article 
data.frame(
  file_name = news_data$file_name,
  content_preview = substr(news_data$content, 1, 100)
)
```
```{r}
if (!requireNamespace("tm", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("tm")
}
```
```{r}
# Load the package
library(tm)
```

```{r}
# Creates text corpus form the article content 
news_corpus <- VCorpus(VectorSource(news_data$content))

# Clean & standardise text 
news_corpus <- tm_map(news_corpus, content_transformer(tolower))
news_corpus <- tm_map(news_corpus, removePunctuation)
news_corpus <- tm_map(news_corpus, removeNumbers)
news_corpus <- tm_map(news_corpus, removeWords, stopwords("english"))
news_corpus <- tm_map(news_corpus, stripWhitespace)

# Add cleaned text to data frame
news_data$cleaned_content <- vapply(
  news_corpus,
  as.character,
  character(1)
)

# Compare original and cleaned text for first article 
data.frame(
  version = c("Original", "Cleaned"),
  preview = c(
    substr(news_data$content[1], 1, 250),
    substr(news_data$cleaned_content[1], 1, 250)
  )
)
```
### Explanation of the preprocessing
The ten news articles were loaded into a data frame, with one row per
document. Each row contains the file name and its corresponding content.
The text was then converted to lowercase, and punctuation, numbers,
common English stopwords and extra whitespace were removed. The original
content was retained alongside the cleaned text for comparison and
subsequent topic modelling.


## Question 2.2: Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA)
```{r}
# Install topicmodels if it is not already installed
if (!requireNamespace("topicmodels", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("topicmodels")
}
```
```{r}
# Load the package
library(topicmodels)
```
```{r}
# Create a document-term matrix from the cleaned corpus
dtm <- DocumentTermMatrix(news_corpus)

# Use the file names as document identifiers
rownames(dtm) <- news_data$file_name

# Check the number of documents and terms
dim(dtm)

# Check that every document contains words
rowSums(as.matrix(dtm))
```
A document-term matrix was created from the preprocessed articles using word counts. An LDA model was then fitted using Gibbs sampling. Three topics were selected as an exploratory starting point, and the ten most probable words were reported for each topic. A fixed random seed was then used to support reproducibility.

```{r}
# Set number of topics 
n_topics <- 3

# Fit LDA model 
lda_model <- LDA(
  dtm,
  k = n_topics,
  method = "Gibbs",
  control = list(seed = 1234)
)

# Display top 10 words for each topic
top_words <- terms(lda_model, 10)
top_words
```
```{r}
# Obtain the topic-word probabilities from the fitted LDA model
topic_word_probabilities <- posterior(lda_model)$terms

# Create a table of the top 10 words and their probabilities
top_word_distribution <- do.call(
  rbind,
  lapply(seq_len(n_topics), function(topic) {
    probabilities <- topic_word_probabilities[topic, ]

    # Select the 10 words with the highest probabilities
    top_indices <- order(probabilities, decreasing = TRUE)[1:10]

    data.frame(
      topic = paste("Topic", topic),
      word = names(probabilities)[top_indices],
      probability = probabilities[top_indices],
      row.names = NULL
    )
  })
)

# Display the results
top_word_distribution
```
### Interpretation of the LDA results
The LDA model was fitted using three topics, and the ten words with the
highest estimated probabilities were displayed for each topic. Topic 1
includes terms such as “department”, “police”, “cold” and “weather”,
suggesting a mixture of public safety and weather-related content.
Topic 2 includes “public”, “service”, “invoices” and “departments”,
suggesting a possible focus on public services and administration.
Topic 3 includes “government”, “coalition”, “eskom” and “power”,
suggesting a possible focus on government and electricity-related news.

The probabilities indicate how likely each word is within its topic,
rather than its raw frequency. Since only the top ten words are shown,
their probabilities do not sum to one. These topic labels are tentative:
the collection contains only ten articles, and some topics contain
words associated with more than one theme.



## Question 2.3: Visualisation of topic keywords

```{r}
# Install ggplot2 if needed
if (!requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("ggplot2")
}

library(ggplot2)

```

```{r}
# Plot the top words and their probabilities for each topic 
ggplot(
  top_word_distribution,
  aes(x = reorder(word, probability), y = probability, fill = topic)
) +
  geom_col(show.legend = FALSE) +
  coord_flip() +
  facet_wrap(~ topic, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Top 10 words in each LDA topic",
    x = "Word",
    y = "Probability within topic"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
```{r}
# Install the wordcloud package 
if (!requireNamespace("wordcloud", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("wordcloud")
}
```

```{r}

library(wordcloud)

# Keep the word placement reproducible
set.seed(1234)

# I chose pink, purple and teal for the top keywords found 
topic_colours <- c(
  "Topic 1" = "#E85D9E",  # Pink
  "Topic 2" = "#9B6ACB",  # Purple
  "Topic 3" = "#2AA6A1"   # Teal
)

# Create one word cloud per topic
for (topic_name in unique(top_word_distribution$topic)) {

  # Select the top words for the current topic
  topic_data <- subset(
    top_word_distribution,
    topic == topic_name
  )

  # Give the cloud some space around its edges
  par(mar = c(1, 1, 3, 1))

  wordcloud(
    words = topic_data$word,
    freq = topic_data$probability,
    scale = c(3, 1),
    min.freq = 0,
    random.order = FALSE,
    rot.per = 0.15,
    colors = topic_colours[topic_name]
  )

  title(
    main = paste("Top keywords:", topic_name),
    col.main = topic_colours[topic_name],
    font.main = 2
  )
}
```
### Interpretation of the visualisations

The bar charts compare the estimated probabilities of the ten most
likely words within each topic. This makes it possible to identify and
compare the most prominent terms in each topic.

The word clouds present the same topic keywords visually. Larger words
have higher estimated probabilities within their respective topics.
Together, the two visualisations provide numerical and visual views of
the words associated with each topic.
